items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: I can estimate Winging Manon too. But these are vastly different people.

ctx.x: Well, does he really have the, does he really, does his music really reflect those, those attitudes of that kind of image that you just described? Or is that something you may be reading into his music? Or that other people are doing?

If I were less sophisticated, I would say that I could be wrong in that. But actually I have investigated so much art, literature, and music. And even though, even though I am illiterate musically, I still have seen enough to satisfy me that this is the case. Because it seems to me that I am one of the people, few as they may be, who can broadly anticipate Biggs' playing. Because I felt that I understood him well enough to know where he would go. And this doesn't in any way detract from my estimate of his…

Wouldn't the Whiteman Orchestra be a better representation of your kind of, your image of that foggy romanticism? And Biggs' playing within the Whiteman Orchestra was an antidote to that kind of saccharine?
